title: Time zones: the session's zone for `TIMESTAMP_LTZ`; a DST gap shifts forward, an overlap takes the earlier offset
verdict: LTZ in the session zone; gap → later wall time; overlap → earlier offset; bad zone raises
description: `TIMESTAMP` is `TIMESTAMP_LTZ` (an instant shown in `spark.sql.session.timeZone`) unless `spark.sql.timestampType` is `TIMESTAMP_NTZ`, as sverify sets it. Text and `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` values become instants in the session zone with `java.time`'s rules: in `America/New_York`, `2024-03-10 02:30` (in the spring gap) becomes 03:30 EDT, and `2024-11-03 01:30` (in the autumn overlap) the earlier offset, EDT (05:30Z).

A string with an offset cast to `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` drops the offset (`'2024-01-05T10:00:00Z'` and `'…+02:00'` both give 10:00). `from_utc_timestamp`, `to_utc_timestamp` and `convert_timezone` shift by a zone's offset; an unknown zone raises `INVALID_TIMEZONE` in both modes.
reference: Time zones are outside the model; sverify's Spark session pins UTC and `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` (`sverify.sql.spark.SPARK_CONF`), so no plan depends on them.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
